items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Actions now provides general availability Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) images, built in partnership with Red Hat. Your organization can use GitHub Actions with the same enterprise-grade Linux environment you use elsewhere, bringing consistency to your CI/CD workflows without requiring workarounds or third-party solutions.

Expected Outcome

We're delivering GA-quality RHEL support to enable enterprise customers to run GitHub Actions workflows on their preferred Linux distribution with full platform parity and support. This eliminates friction for teams already standardized on RHEL and strengthens GitHub Actions as a unified solution for enterprise environments.
items.title: RHEL Actions Runner Images GA [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Copilot SDK 2.0 is a complete rewrite in Rust that delivers significant improvements in performance, extensibility, and portability. With native support for full multi-tenanted applications, developers can now build more scalable Copilot integrations that handle enterprise workloads efficiently.

Expected Outcome

We're making Copilot integration simpler and more powerful for enterprise customers who need to scale their AI-assisted development across multiple teams and organizations. This release removes previous limitations around multi-tenant architectures, enabling businesses to deploy Copilot more broadly within their infrastructure while gaining the reliability and speed that a modern Rust foundation provides.
items.title: Copilot SDK 2.0 [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Secret scanning now works the way you need it to. You can update custom patterns without closing existing alerts, revoke encoded GitHub tokens without decoding them manually, and get more detailed webhook payloads and corrected API responses to build more reliable integrations.

Expected Outcome

We're making secret scanning more flexible and robust for security teams managing custom detection patterns and handling alert workflows at scale. With these updates—including advance notice of upcoming audit log changes—integrations stay aligned with GitHub's security infrastructure as it evolves.
items.title: Secret scanning updates [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Dependabot now supports unauthenticated access to organization-wide private registries, eliminating the need to manage credentials for registries that don't require authentication. This simplifies dependency updates for organizations using anonymous registries, making it easier to keep your codebase secure without extra configuration overhead.

Expected Outcome

We're enabling teams to use Dependabot with registries configured for public access within their organization, reducing setup complexity and allowing developers to focus on dependency management rather than authentication logistics. This expands Dependabot's flexibility to work seamlessly with more registry configurations.
items.title: Dependabot support for unauthenticated organization-wide private registries [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Dependabot withdrawn alerts are now easier to identify using 410 errors and webhooks, so you can automatically close associated external tickets and keep your issue tracking systems in sync with GitHub's security findings.

Expected Outcome

By surfacing withdrawn alerts through API error codes and webhook events, teams can streamline their alert management workflows and reduce manual work when Dependabot alerts are withdrawn or closed.
items.title: Dependabot withdrawn alerts are now easier to identify with 410 errors and webhooks [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Understand your license costs at a glance with a downloadable CSV report showing which repositories and committers are contributing to your overall license spending. This gives you the visibility you need to optimize your use of code quality tools and make informed decisions about your software development spend.

Expected Outcome

We're shipping this feature so customers can make data-driven decisions about their license investments. With clear visibility into which repositories and contributors are generating costs, teams can better manage their development tools budget and allocate resources more effectively across their organization.
items.title: Code Quality license CSV download [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Security Risk Assessments now show you how many secrets and alerts were found in repositories without protection enabled, giving you clear visibility into coverage gaps. This lets you make informed decisions about where to expand your security protection to shield more of your codebase.

Expected Outcome

Customers using GitHub Advanced Security will better understand their protection coverage across their organization and identify which repositories need secret protection or code security enabled. This empowers teams to systematically reduce their security risk by closing visibility gaps and prioritizing protection expansion.
items.title: Security Risk Assessments shows findings are in unprotected repos [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Scheduled code scanning now responds intelligently to your actual development activity. Dormant repositories no longer trigger unnecessary weekly scans, giving you more control over your scanning costs and making security configurations more predictable when applied across your organization.

Expected Outcome

This change creates a tighter connection between your development activity and code scanning behavior. By tying weekly scheduled scans to real push and pull request activity rather than configuration changes or validation runs, you get scanning that works harder when your team is actively shipping code and backs off when a repository goes quiet.
items.title: Scheduled code scanning now reflects push and pull request activity [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Code coverage uploads in GitHub Actions now skip gracefully when pushing to a branch without an open pull request, eliminating workflow failures that used to require manual intervention. Developers can push work-in-progress branches freely, and an Actions notice explains why the upload was skipped, keeping your CI clean and predictable.

Expected Outcome

We're removing friction from developer workflows by making the actions/upload-code-coverage action more resilient to common push scenarios. Developers no longer need to add conditional logic to their workflows to handle non-PR pushes, reducing cognitive load and making code quality practices easier to adopt across teams.
items.title: Code Quality: Code coverage uploads no longer fail CI for branches without a pull request [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Maintainers can now post confidential comments on repository security advisories that are visible only to people with write access to the repository. This keeps sensitive discussions—like suspected abuse, investigation details, or coordination notes—within the advisory itself rather than scattered across email or separate channels, maintaining a complete audit trail while protecting reporter privacy.

Expected Outcome

By enabling confidential team-only comments, we give maintainers a secure way to handle sensitive matters during the advisory process without fragmenting context or losing audit visibility. This addresses a long-standing request from the open source community and brings repository advisories to feature parity with industry-standard vulnerability management platforms that support internal-only discussions.
items.title: Confidential team-only comments on repository security advisories [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Open source maintainers now have the tools to collect structured vulnerability reports with proof of concept and impact information, cutting through noise and speeding up triage. Reporters benefit from clear guidance on exactly what information to provide, and integrations can now submit reports programmatically using the repository's submission template. This transformation reduces the time maintainers spend on low-quality submissions while making it easier for researchers to report vulnerabilities correctly.

Expected Outcome

We're raising the baseline quality of private vulnerability reports by making structured information the default, which helps maintainers focus on legitimate security issues rather than sifting through unverifiable or AI-generated submissions. By requiring proof of concept and other key details upfront, we're reducing friction for serious researchers and helping open source communities respond faster to real security threats.
items.title: Structured, required fields for private vulnerability reports [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Code Scanning now detects indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities in your AI agents and applications during pull requests. You get actionable remediation guidance directly in your workflow, letting you identify and fix risks before they reach production where attackers can exploit them.

Expected Outcome

This release helps development teams safeguard AI-powered systems by catching indirect prompt injection attacks—the top security risk for LLM applications—early in the development cycle. By scanning for risky agent architectures where untrusted content can interact with models that have access to tools and business systems, teams can build more secure AI applications with confidence.
items.title: AI Vulnerabilities scanning on PRs [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Repository admins can now migrate all legacy branch protections on a repository to rulesets in a single action, instead of converting each protection individually. Before committing, a dry-run preview shows exactly which rulesets will be created, which protections are already redundant, and any settings that require special handling — so there are no surprises. This makes it practical to complete the migration to rulesets across your repositories with confidence and far less manual effort.

Expected Outcome

Teams managing branch protections across many repositories have faced a significant barrier to adopting rulesets: the tedious, error-prone process of converting protections one at a time. By enabling bulk migration at the repository level, admins can accelerate their move to rulesets and eliminate the overhead of maintaining two parallel enforcement systems. This release removes a key adoption blocker and sets the stage for org-level bulk migration in a future release.
items.title: Repository-level bulk migration from Branch Protections to Rulesets [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

The async merge API gives you a single, reliable endpoint for merging any pull request — whether it's a direct merge, merge queue, stacked PR, or unstacked PR. You no longer need to track which endpoint to call for each scenario, and merges run asynchronously so they won't time out on large or complex repositories. This makes automating pull request workflows simpler and more resilient.

Expected Outcome

Developers and teams building on the GitHub API can merge pull requests consistently without hitting the 10-second timeout that affects the existing merge endpoints. By consolidating all merge paths into one endpoint, the API becomes easier to adopt and maintain across different repository configurations. This release moves the async merge API from public preview to general availability, making it the recommended approach for programmatic PR merges.
items.title: Async Merge API [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

You can now get AI-powered security findings directly in the code scanning alert backlog alongside your existing CodeQL results — no Actions workflow to set up or maintain, just a single click to enable. AI scanning extends coverage to languages and vulnerability classes that rule-based analysis doesn't reach, so more of your codebase is protected from day one. Findings are deduplicated and reverified automatically, keeping your alert backlog stable, reliable, and low-noise.

Expected Outcome

Developers across every supported language get actionable security coverage without the overhead of configuring or owning a scanning pipeline. By bringing AI-generated findings into the same familiar triage experience as CodeQL alerts, teams can act on a broader set of vulnerabilities without changing how they work. The public preview gives GitHub Advanced Security customers an early path to a more complete and trustworthy security signal across their repositories.
items.title: Code Scanning: full-repo AI scans [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

The global search bar in GitHub navigation now runs on a modern React foundation, giving logged-in users a search experience that looks and feels exactly as before — with no disruption to their workflow. This update brings the search bar into GitHub's unified UI service, enabling faster iteration and richer search capabilities in the future. Developers can continue searching GitHub the same way they always have, with a more reliable and maintainable experience under the hood.

Expected Outcome

Migrating QuickSearch to React consolidates GitHub's global navigation into a single, modern UI framework, removing the complexity of maintaining separate UI stacks. This foundation unblocks the team's ability to build and ship navigation and search improvements more quickly going forward. The outcome is a more consistent, evolvable experience for developers who rely on GitHub's global search every day.
items.title: React-based Quick Search [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Start a session from anywhere in GitHub Mobile—whether you're viewing an issue, pull request, or Actions log—and get a consistent, sandbox-first experience every time. Your repository and relevant context automatically carry over, so you can get to work without extra setup steps.

Expected Outcome

We're standardizing how sessions start across GitHub Mobile to eliminate confusion about where code runs and reduce friction in your workflow. This gives you one predictable way to begin a session from any part of the app, making GitHub Codespaces the clear default while preserving the specific context you need.
items.title: GitHub Mobile: Replace mobile session entry points with the sandbox creation experience [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Enterprise admins can now look up which cost center any user, organization, repository, or team belongs to with a single REST API call—no more scanning through entire cost center lists to find where a resource's usage is charged. This makes billing automation and cost tracking straightforward and efficient.

Expected Outcome

By providing a direct lookup endpoint, enterprises can build accurate billing systems that automatically route usage charges to the correct cost center and give their finance teams visibility into resource costs without manual reconciliation or exhaustive API scans.
items.title: Look up which cost center a resource belongs to via the REST API [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Apps now support enterprise and organization management APIs—including settings, delegated policies, domain verification, two-factor authentication, and bypass requests—letting you retire classic personal access tokens and adopt least-privilege automation. You get more control, better security, and full parity with classic PAT capabilities for enterprise-scale operations.

Expected Outcome

This release helps enterprises and organizations transition away from classic personal access tokens entirely, enabling them to implement stricter security policies and automate administrative workflows using the more secure GitHub Apps authentication model. By filling these API gaps, teams can now standardize on GitHub Apps across their entire automation stack without compromise.
items.title: More Enterprise APIs support GitHub Apps (org/repo settings, enterprise profile, delegated bypass requests) [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Pin your important Copilot sessions and projects on mobile to keep your most-used work front and center. Instead of scrolling through your Copilot feed to find what matters, pinned items stay at the top where you can access them instantly, whether you're on iOS or Android.

Expected Outcome

As teams juggle more sessions and projects, we want to make it easier for you to organize your workflow on mobile. By letting you curate your Copilot tab with pinned items, we're reducing the friction of finding your active work so you can stay focused and productive on the go.
items.title: GitHub Mobile: Pin important Copilot sessions and projects [GA]
